query: What primary balance would Serbia have needed in 2018 to stop its debt-to-GDP ratio from rising?

text.text: Identifies the debt-dynamics identity d_t=(1+lambda)d_{t-1}-p_t with lambda=(r-g)/(1+g) (the debt-stabilising primary balance p*=lambda*d_{t-1}) as the applicable method.
text.accept: full = names the debt-dynamics / debt-stabilising primary balance approach (Escolano 2010; IMF 2013 Staff Guidance Note for public DSA; MAC SRDSF) or applies the equivalent formula; partial = uses only a rule of thumb (r-g)*d without the 1+g denominator; no = uses an overall-balance, structural-balance or S1/S2 method.

data.text: Uses general government gross debt (% GDP), primary balance and overall balance (interest = primary minus overall balance, % GDP), and nominal GDP (WEO Oct 2025: GGXWDG_NGDP, GGXONLB_NGDP, GGXCNL_NGDP, NGDP).
data.accept: full = all inputs correctly sourced; partial = some inputs approximated (e.g. real growth plus deflator); no = unrelated series.

computation.text: Primary balance needed in 2018 is about -1.4% of GDP (a deficit of this size keeps the ratio constant), computed as p* = lambda x previous-year debt with the effective interest rate = interest paid in 2018 / debt at end of 2017 and nominal growth = NGDP_2018/NGDP_2017 - 1; surplus positive.
computation.accept: full = within +-0.20 pp (sign convention: surplus positive; a deficit stated as a positive 'deficit of x' with explicit wording is accepted); partial = right sign within +-0.5 pp; no = otherwise. The gold uses the convention stated in the grading note; interest-definition alternatives (average debt, current-year debt, real-rate form) move the value by at most 0.03 pp, covered by the tolerance. The ratio-of-%GDP-numbers form (interest/GDP_t divided by debt/GDP_{t-1}, no rescaling for GDP growth) moves the value by 0.17 pp and is also covered.

grading.note: Vital computation tolerance +-0.20 (path endpoint pp of GDP; gap/required/horizon-target pp). Verdicts and directions exact. Convention for the gold (WEO Oct 2025, general government): effective interest rate r_t = interest paid in year t divided by gross debt at the end of year t-1 (in levels; interest = primary balance minus overall balance, % of GDP_t, so r_t = interest/GDP_t x (1+g_t) / (debt/GDP)_{t-1}); nominal GDP growth g_t = NGDP_t / NGDP_{t-1} - 1 from nominal GDP in national currency; primary balance = revenue minus non-interest spending, surplus positive; lambda=(r-g)/(1+g) and p* = lambda x (debt/GDP)_{t-1}. Sensitivity: the four interest-definition variants are recorded in the sensitivity object; the tolerance covers them.
grading.definitions: Convention for the gold (WEO Oct 2025, general government): effective interest rate r_t = interest paid in year t divided by gross debt at the end of year t-1 (in levels; interest = primary balance minus overall balance, % of GDP_t, so r_t = interest/GDP_t x (1+g_t) / (debt/GDP)_{t-1}); nominal GDP growth g_t = NGDP_t / NGDP_{t-1} - 1 from nominal GDP in national currency; primary balance = revenue minus non-interest spending, surplus positive; lambda=(r-g)/(1+g) and p* = lambda x (debt/GDP)_{t-1}.

provenance.method_text: Escolano (2010) eqs 5,7,20,22; IMF 2013 Staff Guidance Note (DSA table footnote on debt-stabilising primary balance)

distractors: overall (headline) balance that holds debt constant, b* = -g/(1+g) d (answers a different question)
fiscal-gap or tax-gap indicators (S1/S2) over an infinite horizon
primary balance needed to reach a debt anchor or fiscal-rule ceiling
debt-change decomposition without a stabilising benchmark
answer_summary: SRB 2018: debt prev 55.3, effective rate 3.97%, nominal growth 6.74%, lambda -0.0260, required primary balance -1.44, actual 2.83, gap +4.27. Gold: -1.4
validation_note: The formula is validated on 29 published country-years; item gold is on frozen WEO Oct 2025 data for a historic year, so it is not itself a published number (see published_value_note / published_vintage_note).

definitions.b: interest / average of previous- and current-year debt
definitions.d: real-rate form with GDP-deflator growth and real growth (WEO NGDP_RPCH, NGDP_D)

published_value_note: No DSA baseline table in the corpus states a debt-stabilising primary balance for Serbia for 2018 or an adjacent year: the published figure always refers to the last projection year of the table (report year + 4 or 5), and the validated reports for this country give cd49ff11 (report 2021, last projection year 2026): -1.2.
